diff_attention.What is Differential Attention, and what: It computes attention as the difference of two softmax maps to cancel attention noise on irrelevant context. It targets long-context retrieval and hallucination.
diff_attention.Why subtract two softmax attention maps?: Like a differential amplifier: noise common to both maps cancels, while the signal survives.
diff_attention.How do you split Q and K into two halves: Split Q and K into two halves along the head dimension, compute two softmax maps, subtract lambda times the second, and multiply by V.
diff_attention.How is lambda parameterized and initiali: Reparameterized as exp(q1 . k1) - exp(q2 . k2) + lambda_init, with lambda_init depending on layer depth.
diff_attention.What normalization follows the subtracti: Per-head GroupNorm or RMSNorm, then scale by (1 - lambda_init). The difference changes the statistics of each head.
diff_attention.What does differential attention cost in: Two softmax maps per head at the same total head width, plus a few lambda parameters. Kernels need adapting.
diff_attention.How would you evaluate whether it actual: Check attention mass on the relevant span, needle-in-a-haystack accuracy and hallucination benchmarks against a matched baseline.

mla.What is Multi-Head Latent Attention, and: It compresses keys and values into a shared low-rank latent vector per token, and caches only that latent.
mla.How much KV cache does it save?: The cache per token is the latent plus a small RoPE key, much smaller than full per-head K and V. DeepSeek-V2 reports about 93% savings.
mla.Walk through down-projecting to the late: c = x W_down (dim d_c), then K = c W_uk and V = c W_uv per head. Queries can also be compressed.
mla.Why does RoPE need a separate decoupled: RoPE is position-dependent, so it cannot be absorbed into a fixed up-projection. A separate small rotated key part carries position.
mla.How can the up-projection be absorbed in: q . (c W_uk) = (q W_uk^T) . c, so fold W_uk into the query side and W_uv into the output projection, and attend over latents directly.
mla.MLA versus GQA: quality and memory trade: MLA saves more cache than GQA with similar or better quality, but it is more complex. GQA is simple and widely supported by kernels.
mla.What does MLA cost in compute during dec: More matmul work per token to project into latent space. Decode is usually memory-bound, so trading compute for bandwidth pays.

moe.What is a mixture-of-experts layer, and: Many expert FFNs, and each token uses only k of them. Parameters grow with the expert count while per-token FLOPs stay fixed.
moe.What does the router do?: It scores experts for each token and picks the top-k with mixing weights.
moe.How do you select top-k experts per toke: Softmax over router logits, topk, then renormalize the selected weights (or take the softmax over only the selected logits).
moe.How do you dispatch tokens to experts wi: Sort or group token indices by expert, gather, run each expert on its batch, and scatter back with index_add.
moe.How do you combine expert outputs back i: Multiply each expert's output by the token's routing weight and index_add into the output at the original positions.
moe.What makes MoE training unstable?: Router collapse, load imbalance, large router logits and bf16 rounding. Mention z-loss and balancing losses.
moe.MoE versus a dense model with the same a: MoE has lower compute per quality but needs memory for all experts, plus all-to-all communication and batching complexity.

moe_load_balance.Why do MoE models need a load-balancing: Without pressure, the router sends most tokens to a few experts, wasting capacity and overloading devices.
moe_load_balance.What is routing collapse?: A few experts win early, get more gradient, get better, and win more: a rich-get-richer loop.
moe_load_balance.Write the Switch-style auxiliary loss fr: loss = alpha * E * sum over experts of f_i * P_i. f_i is the fraction of tokens routed to expert i; P_i is the mean router probability for it.
moe_load_balance.Why multiply the fraction by the mean pr: f is non-differentiable (from the argmax). P is differentiable but alone could be gamed. The product is minimized by a uniform distribution.
moe_load_balance.Which term carries gradient?: Only P_i. f_i comes from the hard top-k selection and is treated as a constant.
moe_load_balance.How do you choose the loss weight, and w: Sweep it small, around 1e-2. Too large forces uniform routing and hurts quality because experts cannot specialize.
moe_load_balance.What do auxiliary-loss-free methods such: Add a per-expert bias to the routing scores used for selection only, nudging it up or down according to load (DeepSeek-V3), with no gradient interference.

multi_token_prediction.What is multi-token prediction?: From each position, predict not only the next token but also the tokens 2, 3, ..., N ahead with extra heads.
multi_token_prediction.Why might predicting several future toke: Denser training signal per position and pressure to plan ahead. Reported gains show up on code and at larger scales.
multi_token_prediction.How are the N heads and their targets al: Head k at position t predicts token t + k. Shift the targets by k for each head.
multi_token_prediction.How do you handle positions near the end: Mask positions where t + k runs past the end, or drop the last k positions for head k.
multi_token_prediction.How is the loss averaged across heads?: Average each head's loss over its valid positions, then average (or weight) across heads.
multi_token_prediction.How can MTP heads be used for speculativ: Extra heads propose future tokens and the main model verifies them, as self-speculative drafting.
multi_token_prediction.Where has MTP helped, and where has it n: It helped larger code models (Meta) and DeepSeek-V3's training. Small models and some NLP benchmarks see little or negative change.
